items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 3:39AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Periods of snow are likely today and Friday with southeast winds
gusting up to 45 mph. This will likely result in lowered
visibility to 1 mile or less at times. Temperatures will be
hovering near 32 degrees which means blowing snow will only be
expected when it is actively snowing. Total snow accumulations
around 1 to 3 inches expected through Friday evening.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 2:45AM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
Tidal levels across the panhandle are expected to be running high
for the next few days. These high tides combined with passing low
pressures and their associated fronts could create some
potentially higher than normal water levels. Confidence has
increased for a slightly weaker system moving into the panhandle
during peak tides. Tides may exceed astronomical high tide, though
the likelihood of exceeding a foot has been reduced significantly.
items.areas: City and Borough of Sitka; Western Kupreanof and Kuiu Island; City and Borough of Wrangell; Ketchikan Gateway Borough

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 25 at 9:54PM AKST until November 27 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Blowing Snow. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Central Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...No additional falling snow is expected. Strong
winds will blow snow already on the ground to create areas of low
visibility near the surface. A brief decrease in winds is expected
Wednesday night before winds strengthen once more Thursday.
items.instruction:
Use caution while traveling, especially in open areas. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 10:30AM AKST until November 28 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding with water levels 1.5 to 3.0 feet above
the highest tide line possible.

* WHERE...Kipnuk and Kwigillingok

* WHEN...6 PM Thursday to 6 AM Saturday. Particularly the
overnight tide cycles Thursday night and Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Potential flooding of low lying areas, including
lowest portions of boardwalks. Coastal erosion possible.
